newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia sets land values, leases.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia sets land values, leases.

text.p: The Mongolian government has made an official assessment of land values and leases, the Government News said on Wednesday.

Land in the capital was valued at 440 million tugriks per hectare ($551,911), and at 300 million, 200 million and 120 million per hectare in the cities of Darkhan, Erdenet and Choibalsan, the newspaper said.
Land leases in the capital ranged between 440,000 tugriks and 4.4 million tugriks per hectare per year while they ranged from 120,000 to 900,000 tugriks in the other three cities.
Land in smaller towns and villages was also included in the assessment.
Mongolian law says land in cities, towns and villages may be privatised, but pasture land remains state property.
The country has not yet begun land privatisation on a large scale though the capital of Ulan Bator auctioned three small plots for commercial use in May.
The state newspaper did not explain the assessment, but analysts said the officially set land value could be used as a starting point for future auctions.
Present laws allow only citizens of Mongolia to own land, although foreigners may lease land for five-year terms.
